title: Patriots make roster move with rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas
description: The Patriots have reportedly placed rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas on the active/non-football injury list.
fullText:
The New England Patriots have placed rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas on the active/non-football injury list. ESPN's Mike Reiss reported the news on Sunday.

This news comes after the Patriots finally came to a contract agreement with Jacas, who missed all of the team's spring practices. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel indicated that the team would be cautious with Jacas considering the time missed and the fact that he is working his way back from multiple injuries.

Going on the NFI list means that Jacas is not ready to practice at this time, but that status can change at any moment. The Patriots probably hope it's sooner rather than later given their questionable depth at edge rusher. Harold Landry is currently on the PUP list, leaving the unit down to Dre'Mont Jones, Bradyn Swinson, Elijah Ponder and Jesse Luketa.

Follow-up: After officially signing second-round pick Gabe Jacas, the Patriots placed him on the active/non-football injury list.

Head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would take a cautious approach. 

This reflects that Jacas is not yet ready to practice. Can change any day.

— Mike Reiss (@MikeReiss) July 26, 2026

Jacas is a player talented enough to come in and help right away.

But how far along is he in learning the defense? He missed crucial time in the development process, and now, he'll have to play catch-up behind the rest of the rookies.

title: REPORT: Browns Exploring Edge Rusher Additions Ahead of Camp
description: After the blockbuster trade of Myles Garrett, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry is hunting for a veteran defensive end to solidify a new-look front before training camp commences.
fullText:
Training camp may be just days away for the Cleveland Browns, but the roster tweaking never stops for Executive Vice President of Football Operations Andrew Berry.

Berry already pulled off a blockbuster trade earlier this summer to send Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for a handful of picks and on-the-rise edge rusher Jared Verse. He may be looking to bolster the position even more with training camp ramping up.

According to Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com, the Browns are apparently in the market for another edge rusher.

"The Browns are still in the market for a veteran defensive end to add to the rotation and make up for the loss of former Bills edge rusher A.J. Epenesa, who failed his physical," wrote Cabot on Sunday.

She added that Cleveland would prefer to find this mystery edge rusher before training camp commences on Wednesday, but that it may take some time to actually identify someone and sign them.

Cleveland Browns Offseason Report; Which Brown is set for breakout? | Roster rankings fair or foul? The Cleveland Browns are just two weeks away from reporting to camp and then the season will be on for the Browns. Until then, it is another conversation abo...

As Cabot noted, at one point this offseason the Browns were set to sign Buffalo Bills free agent Epenesa to a contract, but balked after being uncomfortable with something that popped up during his physical.

Several months later, the former second-round pick wound up signing a one-year deal with the Philadelphia Eagles instead.

As things stand right now, the Browns boast a pretty strong starting front four along the defensive line, headlined by the newly acquired Verse. The unit also includes veteran DT Maliek Collins, 2025, No. 5 overall pick Mason Graham and 2022 third-round pick Alex Wright.

Behind those four, though, the Browns would benefit from some additional depth for rotational purposes. Cleveland will sorely miss Garrett, for obvious reasons, but building a deeper defensive line that can collectively attempt to make up for what's lost in Garrett's absence could certainly help matters.

Of course, Verse will carry the heaviest burden to replicate as much as he can, Garrett's impact, granted nobody should expect him to be the two-time Defensive Player of the Year.

He won't have to go it alone, though, and another addition to the room will only help ease some of the pressure on him, hence why adding another veteran is of the utmost importance to Berry and company. It sounds like it's just a matter of when, rather than if, Cleveland will be adding another edge rusher to their roster.

title: Corey's time is now and 23XI think they already have a superstar
description: Heim is now in the AJ Foyt, Tim Richmond and Davey Allison territory
fullText:
Heim Time is so incredibly ahead of schedule.

On May 30, 23XI Racing revealed that Corey Heim would finally compete full-time in the NASCAR Cup Series. Since then, all he’s done is look like a legitimate championship contender for a division he isn’t even fully delved into yet.

Over the past five weeks, he’s won twice, at Naval Base North Island and now the Brickyard 400 at Indianapolis Motor Speedway. That doesn’t even include his three Truck Series wins in six starts this season.

The 23-year-old from Marietta, Georgia isn’t an emerging superstar because he already looks like one six months before his inaugural full-time campaign. Bootie Barker, his crew chief, says Heim is simply already one of the best drivers in the division, right now, no argument.

“I think everybody thinks I'm always joking but he's more talented than everybody else,” Barker said. “That’s almost a disservice to some of the great drivers here (but) that's not the case.

"Like all the people we were racing at the end are the best of the best, tremendous. Show much respect to them but Corey is there in talent. Corey is also there in work ethic. He's there as far as a mentality. He has all that now. That's no guarantee going forward, but right now he has it.”

Heim has won twice in eight starts this year, and if it wasn’t for the car not having full-time status, allowing them to qualify even better each week, Barker says they’d have enjoyed even more success.

“If we would have had a better metric in qualifying, we would have won more already,” Barker said.

During the 23XI Racing and Front Row Motorsports v NASCAR antitrust lawsuit, a text message exchange between team owners Denny Hamlin and Michael Jordan was made public, in which the former said they needed to sign Heim to a multiyear deal.

Jordan said ‘lock him up,’ something they successfully executed this past summer. Team president Steve Lauletta said this is early validation.

“Bootie mentioned it, Denny has many times before,” said Lauletta. “That's why Denny has had his eye on him and why Toyota has invested in Corey as much. His approach, his work ethic, his race craft. Just the amount of discipline that he has and maturity that he has just really shows in all of his preparation.

“The relationship he's built with everybody at (the shop) (and) with the other drivers. I just think he's mature beyond his years and it's showing in a very quick way.”

Now, there was a little fortune involved in winning the Brickyard 400 on Sunday, but that is generally the case on Sundays every week. Heim lost the lead when Joey Logano attempted to take him and Denny Hamlin three-wide on the penultimate restart but the three-time champion then pushed him ahead when it mattered the most.

“As we wound down, I was sitting there talking to my spotter Eddie (D’Hondt) and crew chief Bootie,” Heim said. “They both just said, ‘We got to muscle up on this restart’ (and) ‘This is more than likely going to decide the outcome of the race.’

“That was before Denny got the lead on me. Joey tried to put me three there, kill both of our momentum. That got Denny the lead. I thought that was potentially the race. Got another caution. ‘Here we go, might have a shot at it.’ Then Joey gave me a really good push up front.”

And just like that, Heim has won twice in 15 part-time starts, all before his first full-time season. This is something that hasn’t been accomplished since Davey Allison and Tim Richmond won races on a part-time basis in 1987.

Heim is also the first driver to win two of his first 15 starts since AJ Foyt in 1965.

“I'm not much of a stats guy honestly,” Heim said. “Sounds like it's a pretty good one. Definitely cool to be included with a guy like that. Been a crazy year so far. To win two of my first 15 is something I never thought I would accomplish, but here we are. It's a crazy feeling.”

And one of them is a crown jewel that has been won by the likes of Jeff Gordon, Dale Earnhardt, Bill Elliott, Dale Jarrett, Kevin Harvick, Tony Stewart and Jimmie Johnson. Heim is now on that list before he even gets a chance to go points racing next year.

“It's cool to talk about, I guess,” Heim said in his own understated kind of way. “I don't really ever keep up with how many crown jewel wins most guys have, I guess.

“Yeah, I mean, just to be able to win it for myself is just insane. Just super thankful for 23XI, Toyota, everyone that put me in position to do this. Hopefully cross some more off in my career. Who knows, maybe we can win all of them one day. We'll see.”

Again, at this point, he’s ahead of schedule so the sky is the limit.

title: Lamine Yamal ‘not really on holiday’ as Barcelona star’s training regime revealed

fullText:
Lamine Yamal is enjoying some time off after a long season with Barcelona was followed by a trip to the USA, Mexico and Canada for the World Cup with Spain.

The teenager ended up helping La Roja win the tournament to add the World Cup to his growing list of titles.

Yamal has now been given three weeks off, along with his Spain team-mates, and has been holidaying with girlfriend Ines Garcia.

Yet she has been happy to show off on Instagram how Yamal is sticking to his training regime (and still wearing his Spain training kit) by posting some videos with the caption: “In reality we’re not really on vacation…”

MAROA, Ill. (WCIA) — Before sending athletes off on one last summer break, Maroa-Forsyth hosted local schools for some friendly competition.

The Trojans hosted their 26th annual 7-on-7 Tournament and Lineman Challenge, welcoming in Clinton, Eureka, Pontiac, Peoria Notre Dame and other schools for a day of competition. Each team was guaranteed three games with two twenty-minute halves.

Maroa-Forsyth head coach Josh Jostes praised the turnout, glad to see teams continuing to challenge their athletes during the offseason.

“Well, just glad to see the game of football still strong,” Jostes said. “There are plenty of kids out here and man, what a great day for weather. fullText:
For the second time this month, the Chicago White Sox and Pittsburgh Pirates paired up on a trade.

The Sox acquired right-handed pitcher José Urquidy from the Pirates on Sunday for minor-league pitcher Félix Doroteo.

Urquidy, 31, went 0-1 with an 8.53 ERA and six strikeouts over 6 1/3 innings during five relief appearances for the Pirates from March 29-April 13. He went 5-4 with a 3.66 ERA and 73 strikeouts in 83 2/3 innings in 17 starts with Triple-A Indianapolis.

He was designated for assignment by Pittsburgh on Friday.

Urquidy is 27-17 with a 4.07 ERA and 335 strikeouts in 413 2/3 innings during 86 appearances (70 starts) over seven big-league seasons with the Houston Astros (2019-23), Detroit Tigers (2025) and Pirates (2026).

Doroteo, 21, is 3-2 with a 4.50 ERA and 24 strikeouts in 19 innings over 16 outings (one start) with the Arizona Complex League White Sox this year, his first professional season. He was signed by the Sox as an international free agent on Jan. 15, 2025.

The Sox and Pirates are becoming familiar trade partners. On July 10, the Sox sent infielder Jacob Gonzalez and pitcher Brandon Eisert to Pittsburgh for a Competitive Balance Round A selection (No. 34 overall) in the draft and left-handed pitcher Jaden Woods. The Sox selected Nazareth infielder Landon Thome with the pick the next day.

After Sunday’s trade, the Sox’s 40-man roster increased to 39. The MLB trade deadline is Aug. 3.

The Kansas City Chiefs posted a video of Patrick Mahomes and the QB room throwing passes during training camp. It featured the two-time NFL MVP, along with Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun.

They all passed quickly, showcasing that they are in good shape ahead of the 2026 season. Mahomes continues to recover from the torn ACL he sustained in December but looks sharp and not hampered by his injury. The quarterback battle in training camp is expected to be fierce and competitive.

The clip on X has since gone viral, with more than two million views.

Mahomes will reportedly be ready to return as early as Week 1. However, Kansas City is not taking any chances and brought in Justin Fields from the New York Jets to serve as insurance at the position. He has 53 career NFL starts under his belt and will likely be the team’s QB2 once the three-time Super Bowl champion is back to full strength.

Fields joined the Chiefs on March 18 after the franchise sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to New York. They then drafted Nussmeier at No. 249 overall in the seventh round out of LSU. The former Tigers star spent five years with the program and went 5-4 last season.

The Pittsburgh Steelers waived Oladokun in 2022, but he signed a practice squad deal with Kansas City. The team promoted him to the active roster on Dec. 20 following Mahomes’ injury the week prior, and he started his first NFL game on Christmas Day against the Denver Broncos.

The Chiefs will likely ease Mahomes back before he takes over his QB1 job full-time. Fields will serve as his backup, while Nussmeier and Oladokun will battle for the third-string role.

title: Pirates Problems: Buccaneers Looking for Revenge Against Falcons
description: Haunted by a collapse on "3rd and 28," Tampa Bay targets divisional redemption. New coordinator Zac Robinson and quarterback Baker Mayfield seek personal vengeance against their former employers.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will likely have to do well in each of their six divisional matchups if they are to finish the season as NFC South champions.

Tampa split each of their series against the Carolina Panthers, Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints last season. Had they won just one more game, the Bucs would have won the division instead of narrowly missing out of the playoffs.

The three divisional losses were by a combined eight points, and the one against Atlanta is probably the most painful.

Any Buccaneers fan is aware of "3rd and 28," as well as coach Todd Bowles' profanity-laced tirade that followed Atlanta's 29-28 win on Thursday Night Football.

Tampa's first chance at revenge against Atlanta will take place Sunday, Nov. 1, at Raymond James Stadium, the scene of the crime. From Atlanta's perspective, the Thursday Night win proved to be a launching pad. The Falcons came into that matchup 4-9, and after beating Tampa, they won their last three games to finish 8-9, tied for the best record in the NFC South.

Although Atlanta lost out on the division championship due to a tiebreaker, the Falcons ended the season flying high. The same can't be said for Tampa Bay, which looked to be a lock to win the South when it was 6-2, but ended up losing seven of its last nine. Things will have to be different in 2026 for Bowles to silence his critics, and they already look different.

Two days after the end of the regular season, Tampa fired offensive coordinator Josh Grizzard after just one season. Tampa replaced Grizzard with the man who engineered "3rd and 28."

The Falcons' late surge wasn't enough to save head coach Raheem Morris' job. When Morris got fired and new head coach Kevin Stefanski came in, Stefanski understandably wanted his guys on staff, including the offensive coordinator.

That made Zac Robinson a free agent, and the Bucs took advantage.

So come November, Robinson will be taking on his former team, and Robinson's quarterback, Baker Mayfield, will be taking on his former head coach.

Stefanski was Cleveland's boss when Mayfield led the Cleveland Browns to their only playoff win since the "new Browns" emerged in 1999.

He was also Cleveland's boss when the Browns made the now-infamous DeShaun Watson trade 14 months later and essentially kicked Mayfield to the curb.

Mayfield hasn't forgotten how things ended in Cleveland, and made it clear that he's no Kevin Stefanski fan.

Beating the Falcons would make a lot of people happy, perhaps Mayfield most of all.

title: Angels hold off late Giants rally, avoid sweep at Oracle Park
description: Jose Soriano held the Giants at bay for five innings, and the Angels survived a ninth-inning scare to escape Oracle Park with a 4-3 win and avoid the sweep.
fullText:
SAN FRANCISCO — A day after getting buried in one of their ugliest losses of the season, the Angels needed length from a starter and a little popfrom the middle of the order. They got both, then had to survive one more scare before it counted.

Los Angeles avoided a three-game sweep at Oracle Park, holding off a late Giants rally for a 4-3 win Sunday that included Mike Trout's first four-hit game since 2021 and Mitch Farris' first career save.

The Angels struck first in the top of the first, when Trout doubled, moved to third on a wild pitch and scored on a Jorge Soler groundout. It held up as the only run for two innings, with Jose Soriano working around traffic and keeping San Francisco off the board behind him.

Jul 26, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Angels center fielder Mike Trout (27) celebrates his double against the San Francisco Giants during the first inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: D. Ross Cameron-Imagn Images

Soriano gave the Angels exactly what was missing a day earlier. The right-hander worked five innings and allowed just one run on three hits while striking out five to improve to 9-6, settling in after a shaky opening stretch and giving the bullpen a game it could actually manage.

The offense broke it open in the fourth. Soler led off the inning with a home run, his 12th of the year, and after Nolan Schanuel walked, Jo Adell followed with a two-run shot to center that pushed the lead to 4-0.

Jul 26, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Angels right fielder Jo Adell (7) celebrates his two-run home run against the San Francisco Giants during the fourth inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: D. Ross Cameron-Imagn Images

San Francisco started clawing back in the fifth. Willy Adames doubled and came around to score on a force-out at second that included a throwing error by Zach Neto, cutting the lead to 4-1. It was as far as the Giants would get until things got interesting late in the game. Samy Natera Jr., Chase Silseth and Ryan Zeferjahn combined to hold the Giants there through the eighth, setting up a ninth inning the Angels couldn't afford to give away.

Sam Bachman opened the frame by walking two batters around a force out, and Farris came on to try to clean it up. He nearly didn't get the chance. Pinch-hitter Daniel Susac lined out, but Luis Arraez ripped a double off the right field wall that scored both of Bachman's inherited runners and pulled the Giants within 4-3. Heliot Ramos, out of replay challenges, went down looking on a call that appeared to catch the inside corner, and the Angels held on to their win.

Jul 26, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Angels catcher Logan O'Hoppe (14) and pitcher Mitch Farris (70) celebrate defeating the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: D. Ross Cameron-Imagn Images

Trout finished 4-for-4, Soler and Adell each drove in two, and Soriano's bounce-back outing kept Los Angeles from a fourth straight loss to close out the series. Carson Whisenhunt took the loss for San Francisco, allowing four runs on five hits with two homers over five innings.

The win also snapped a stretch where Los Angeles hadn't looked like itself, coming a day after a blowout loss that had San Francisco threatening to sweep the series. Sunday's version of the Angels looked nothing like Saturday's.

The Angels head home to open a three-game set against Houston on Monday, with Walbert Ureña opposing Tatsuya Imai at 6:38 p.m. PT.

title: Aces add another player heading off to FIBA World Cup
description: While the Las Vegas Aces are expected to be heavy contributors to the rosters for the 2026 FIBA World Cup, another lesser-known player is going back to represent her country once again.
fullText:
While the Las Vegas Aces are expected to be heavy contributors to the rosters for the 2026 FIBA World Cup, another lesser-known player is going back to represent her country once again.

On Sunday, it was confirmed that Aces forward Stephanie Talbot would be a part of Team Australia for the World Cup, which is set to go from Sept. 4-13 in Berlin.

It has been something of a challenging season for Talbot in her first go-around in Las Vegas, averaging only 3.5 points and three rebounds per game despite starting all but one of her 26 games and averaging 18.5 minutes.

However, Talbot’s international experience was what drew interest from the Aces, and Australia boasts one of the top women’s basketball teams in the world, with their most recent triumph being a bronze medal at the 2024 Olympics.

More holdovers from that bronze medal team include head coach Sandy Brondello (Toronto Tempo), as well as Isobel Borlase (Atlanta Dream), Ezi Magbegor (Seattle Storm), Jade Melbourne (Seattle), Alanna Smith (Dallas Wings) and Sami Whitcomb (Phoenix Mercury). The team is also confirmed to include another WNBA player in Chloe Bibby (Chicago Sky) to their ranks.

Talbot has been a part of Team Australia since 2015, participating in three Olympics and two World Cups so far. She played a part in the Australians taking home silver medals in the 2018 World Cups and bronze in the 2022 rendition, where she was also named to the All-Star five of the tournament.

Back in somewhat more familiar and friendlier territory, a good tournament could be what Talbot needs to find her footing and gain some momentum when the Aces begin their likely playoff push.

title: Britain's Jones defends Challenger title in Palermo
description: Britain's Francesca Jones makes it back-to-back wins on the Challenger Tour by successfully defending her title at the Palermo Ladies Open.
fullText:
Britain's Francesca Jones made it back-to-back wins on the Challenger Tour by successfully defending her title at the Palermo Ladies Open.

The top seed beat Fiona Ferro 6-0 4-6 7-6 (8-6) in two hours and 43 minutes.

Jones, who had dropped one set all tournament, took the opener in just 21 minutes.

The 25-year-old then fought back from 3-0 down to lead 4-3 in the second, but Ferro reeled off three straight games to level the match.

A tight deciding set went all the way to a tie break, where the French seventh seed spurned match point at 6-5, allowing Jones to close out victory.

It was her fourth career win on the Challenger Tour and second in eight days, following a victory at the ATV Rome Open.

"We both deserved to win. It was a close match until the end, and we did everything we could," said Jones, who beat Anouk Koevermans of the Netherlands to win the title in 2025.

fullText:
Wales attacking midfielder Harry Wilson made his first outing for Leeds United as they were beaten 3-2 by Wrexham in the club's opening pre-season game.

Wilson, who joined the Elland Road side on a free transfer in the summer after his contract at Fulham ran out, came on for the second half of the game at the Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.

Leeds found themselves behind almost immediately when Kieffer Moore put Wrexham in front in the first minute with a left-foot shot.

Joel Piroe had the chance to level from the spot after Dan James had been brought down by keeper Arthur Okonkwo, but missed with his penalty.

Piroe made amends for the Premier League side by equalising with a backheel from a Sean Longstaff ball.

Bailey Cadamarteri ran through on goal and slotted in to put Wrexham back in front before Leeds again levelled when Longstaff scored with a right-footed shot.

Wilson was introduced by Leeds manager Daniel Farke as part of his changes for a second half in which Sam Smith, who also scored Wrexham's winner in a pre-season victory against Manchester United, netted late on for the Championship side.

title: Spence Jr to retire after losing comeback fight
description: Former welterweight world champion Errol Spence Jr will retire from boxing after losing his comeback fight to Tim Tszyu in Sydney.
fullText:
Former welterweight world champion Errol Spence Jr has retired from boxing after losing his comeback fight to Tim Tszyu in Sydney.

American Spence Jr, 36, held the WBA, WBC and IBF belts and was undefeated in 28 fights before being beaten by Terence Crawford three years ago.

His first fight back saw him on the back foot throughout against Australian Tszyu, losing 118-110, 117-111, 117-111 on points.

"I think yeah, for sure," Spence said when asked if this was the end of the road for his career.

"I've got my faculties intact. My money is good at working for itself. Everything's good, man.

"I've got a beautiful family, and I thank God I'm gracious to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family still by my side."

Tszyu grew in confidence and power throughout the fight and consistently looked to attack Spence's chin. He now wants a shot at a title of his own.

"I had sleepless nights thinking about, 'What am I going to feel like facing a legend like that?' But it was one hell of a show, and I understand why he's one of the greats," Tszyu said.

"I'd love to fight for a title. That's what I'm aiming for. But I've got to say beating a great like Errol Spence tops a world title."

Spence won his first title in 2017 when he beat British fighter Kell Brook at Bramall Lane.

title: DNS Service Binding (SVCB) and HTTPS Records: A Practical Guide
description: In my previous post on encrypted DNS, I mentioned SVCB and HTTPS records together. For encrypted DNS discovery specifically, it is SVCB, used with the DNS-server mapping in RFC 9461 and DDR in RFC 9462, that lets supporting clients discover encrypted resolver transports without a manually entered DoH URL. I got several follow-up questions asking what these records actually are, how they work, what problems they solve, and what new problems they create.
fullText:
In my previous post on encrypted DNS, I mentioned SVCB and HTTPS records together. For encrypted DNS discovery specifically, it is SVCB, used with the DNS-server mapping in RFC 9461 and DDR in RFC 9462, that lets supporting clients discover encrypted resolver transports without a manually entered DoH URL. I got several follow-up questions asking what these records actually are, how they work, what problems they solve, and what new problems they create.

This is a deep dive into both. I'll explain the mechanics, show you how they work with real examples you can test, walk through their legitimate use cases, and then discuss the operational challenges they present, especially for organisations trying to maintain control over encrypted DNS at their perimeter.

I make no secret of the fact that I love DNS. I think it's one of the most fascinatingly simple yet powerful protocols in the internet stack. The strength of DNS is its flexibility to do things that the original designers never imagined, while its biggest weakness is its flexibility to do things that the original designers never imagined. SVCB and HTTPS records are a perfect example of both sides of that coin.

SVCB and HTTPS records are fundamentally different from the DNS records you're used to. They're not just another way to signpost from a domain to a server IP address. They're a service metadata layer that lets DNS tell clients which endpoints to use, which protocols those endpoints support, and how to connect to them. That flexibility is powerful. It's also why they've become a vector for unexpected behaviour in networks trying to enforce encrypted DNS policies.

Let's start with what they are and how they work.

Before RFC 9460 (November 2023), connecting to HTTPS services was surprisingly inefficient. Here's what happened:

Many sites still serve HTTP on port 80 and redirect to HTTPS. So your browser makes an HTTP request, gets a 301 redirect to https://example.com, then opens a TLS connection on port 443. That's already two round trips before any data flows.

Then the browser connects on HTTP/2, the server responds with an Alt-Svc header saying "hey, I also support HTTP/3", and the browser opens a new connection on QUIC. That's a third round trip. Multiple negotiations when one should have done the job.

Zone apex caused another headache. You couldn't use CNAME at example.com, only subdomains worked. This meant delegating your whole domain to a CDN was complicated. You had to either break your email routing or use hacky workarounds. The SVCB/HTTPS family fixed this for participating clients.

SVCB and HTTPS records let you move a lot of that connection metadata into DNS. Capable clients can learn supported protocols, preferred endpoints, and sometimes address hints before they connect. That can reduce redirects, avoid the Alt-Svc dance, and cut down on some follow-up lookups, but it does not magically eliminate every extra query in every implementation.

A generic SVCB record looks like this:

Priority (the 1 here) tells clients which record to try first. Lower numbers win. Priority 0 is special: it means "use this as an alias" (we'll get to that).

Endpoint (the resolver.example.com part) is where the service actually lives.

Parameters (the alpn="h2,h3" and dohpath="/dns-query{?dns}" bits) tell clients what protocols the endpoint supports and, for DoH, which URI template to use.

The important relationship is this: SVCB is the generic mechanism, while HTTPS is the SVCB-compatible RR type specialized for HTTPS origins. Because HTTPS already implies the https scheme, web clients query the origin name directly:

Two useful bits of shorthand: RR type 65 is HTTPS, so dig HTTPS example.com is the readable way to query it. And in DNS-server SVCB records, key7 is the parameter code for dohpath.

Generic SVCB is service-agnostic, so its owner name comes from the protocol mapping for that service, usually with underscored labels such as _dns.resolver.example.com.

SVCB query names come from the protocol mapping for the service you are describing. A common pattern is an underscored scheme label, and sometimes an extra port prefix for non-default ports:

The underscore prefix prevents conflicts with ordinary hostnames. A client looking for _dns.resolver.example.com will not accidentally match resolver.example.com itself. This service-awareness means you can describe different protocols cleanly without overloading the base hostname.

For your main web service on the default HTTPS port, you do not use prefix labels. Just use the HTTPS record at your origin name:

The HTTPS RR type is the specialized web variant, so it avoids the underscore label for ordinary https://example.com origins. If you are describing some other service, or HTTPS on a non-default port, the mapping-defined underscored name comes back into play.

AliasMode uses priority 0 and works like CNAME but only for the RR type being queried. For a web origin at the apex, that means HTTPS 0:

The clever part? You can publish this and keep your MX records for email. Web clients query HTTPS; mail clients query MX. CNAME would not let those coexist at the same owner name.

ServiceMode uses priority 1 or higher and describes a specific endpoint with its parameters. You can have multiple ServiceMode records:

Clients prefer priority 1 first, then 2, then 3. The service metadata arrives up front, although clients may still need follow-up address lookups depending on the target names and resolver behavior.

Browser support is real, but it is not uniform.

The practical rule is simple: publish HTTPS records as an optimization layer, not as the only mechanism keeping your site secure or fast.

This was a painful problem before SVCB and HTTPS. You want to delegate your apex domain to a CDN, but you still need mail servers. CNAME will not work at the apex.

Now web clients that understand HTTPS records can follow the web alias, while mail and SPF lookups still use the MX and TXT records at the same owner name.

Why HTTPS AliasMode wins over CNAME at the apex:

Before HTTPS AliasMode, operators had to use workarounds: either put the apex on their own servers and proxy to the CDN, or move the site to a subdomain. HTTPS AliasMode makes the web part work correctly, although legacy clients still need ordinary A/AAAA fallback.

HTTP/3 (QUIC) is faster and more resilient than HTTP/2, especially on slow or unstable networks. But clients don't know you support it without trial and error.

Old way: Browser connects on HTTP/2, server sends Alt-Svc header, browser waits, then reconnects on HTTP/3. Multiple round trips, extra latency.

New way: Your HTTPS record says it upfront:

Clients that support it can see this in DNS and attempt HTTP/3 immediately instead of waiting to learn about it from Alt-Svc after the first connection.

Imagine you're operating a global service across multiple providers. You use one CDN as the preferred endpoint and another as a fallback. Traditionally you might reach for GeoDNS or BGP-heavy solutions.

With HTTPS, you can publish multiple endpoints in operator-preference order:

Clients typically try the lowest priority first and can fail over if it is unavailable. That makes the record set useful for multi-endpoint failover and delegated service metadata. It is not a magic replacement for GeoDNS, though: geography comes from how those target names resolve and where those services live, not from SvcPriority itself.

This is where things get interesting for enterprise security. As I covered in the encrypted DNS post and mentioned at the start of this post, SVCB records are the key to encrypted DNS discovery. When a client initially knows only a plaintext resolver IP, it can query _dns.resolver.arpa for SVCB records to learn about encrypted transports and parameters. This means you need to be careful if you want to maintain control over encrypted DNS at your network perimeter, but it also means that supporting clients can discover DoH and DoT without a manually entered DoH URL. In practice you want to publish your own path to your own resolver when you come to support DoH or DoT, but also block other domain specific SVCB records to prevent auto-discovery of external DoH endpoints.

To test this, and assuming you have a recent version of dig, here is a special query every client can make:

This asks Cloudflare's resolver: "What's your encrypted endpoint?" And it responds:

Try it yourself, the above is slightly simplified because Cloudflare also includes ipv4hint and ipv6hint parameters, but the key point is the same.

Translation: priority 1 advertises a DoH-capable endpoint using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, and priority 2 advertises DoT.

Understanding the dohpath parameter (key7):

The key7="/dns-query{?dns}" part is the DoH path template. It tells clients how to construct a DoH request:

Different providers use different paths:

For IP-bootstrap DDR via _dns.resolver.arpa, there is one subtlety from RFC 9462: the client starts from the resolver IP it already knows. The SVCB data tells it which encrypted transports, ports, authentication names, and DoH path template are valid, but the bootstrap context still matters.

The bootstrap trust problem: The SVCB response arrives over plaintext DNS, so it cannot be trusted blindly. Before upgrading, the client must verify that the advertised DoH/DoT server actually controls the original resolver IP. It does this by checking the TLS certificate: the certificate presented by the encrypted endpoint must include the original plaintext resolver IP as a Subject Alternative Name (SAN). If it does not match, the client refuses to upgrade. This prevents an attacker on the plaintext path from redirecting DNS to a rogue encrypted resolver.

Windows DDR support: Microsoft co-authored the DDR specification and shipped support in Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022. You can enable it with:

Once enabled, the only plaintext DNS traffic on port 53 should be the DDR SVCB queries themselves. All other queries go over the discovered DoH connection. Set ddrfallback=yes if you want Windows to fall back to plaintext when DDR fails. Quad9 (9.9.9.9), OpenDNS (146.112.41.2), and Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) all support DDR discovery on their resolvers.

A significant gap on the server side: Windows DNS Server does not support SVCB or HTTPS record types, so you cannot use it to publish _dns.resolver.arpa records for your own internal resolver. If you are running a Windows DNS infrastructure and want to offer DDR to your clients, the most elegant workaround is to create a conditional forwarder for resolver.arpa pointing at a BIND instance that serves the SVCB records. Not ideal, but it works until Microsoft adds SVCB support to the server side.

If the resolver name is already known, you would publish something like this:

With a supporting client and the right DDR validation model, that can move a device from plaintext bootstrap DNS to an encrypted resolver without a manually entered DoH URL. Powerful, but not unconditional or universal.

SVCB and HTTPS are not only about ALPN and ports. The design is meant to carry richer connection metadata, which is why these records matter to browser and CDN teams.

One example is Encrypted Client Hello (ECH), which aims to hide more of the TLS handshake metadata from passive observers. That sits slightly outside the core RFCs this post is focused on, so I am not going deep on the exact parameter definitions here.

I have touched on SNI headers in the past and how they leak metadata, sometimes in a useful way like with firewall FQDN filtering without TLS inspection. ECH is an alternative to ESNI that encrypts the SNI and other handshake metadata, but it also requires clients to learn about ECH support through some out-of-band mechanism. SVCB and HTTPS records are a natural fit for that discovery, and some providers are already using them to advertise ECH support.

The important architectural point is that HTTPS records are a delivery mechanism for connection policy, not just a shortcut to HTTP/3. Once a client trusts that RRset, DNS can influence much more than which transport gets tried first.

What's happening here: priority 1 says "use DoH with HTTP/2 or HTTP/3". The ipv4hint and ipv6hint parameters can help clients avoid some follow-up address lookups when they honour them. Priority 2 offers DoT (DNS over TLS) as an alternative.

Google's RRset gives DoT priority 1 and DoH priority 2. The priorities express the operator's preference; the client still has to support the advertised transports.

That . means "use cloudflare.com itself" (not a different endpoint). The browser learns upfront that Cloudflare advertises HTTP/3. The address hints may let some clients skip follow-up address lookups, but they are still advisory.

If you're using Cloudflare in proxied mode, it's probably already publishing HTTPS records for you. If you want to set this up for your own domain, here are the steps:

Make sure you have a recent version of dig that supports SVCB and HTTPS record types. Older versions ignore it completely, but you can still test with online tools or your browser's developer tools.

Most DNS providers now support SVCB and HTTPS records. Cloudflare, AWS Route 53, DNSimple, Akamai, and Google Cloud DNS all have it. Check your provider's UI or API.

For a basic HTTP/3-enabled domain:

If you are using a separate target name, you can add address hints so capable clients may skip some follow-up address lookups:

You should get your record back. If nothing appears, check that your provider supports the record type or wait for DNS caching to clear.

If you don't have dig installed locally, use these browser-based tools instead:

Query different resolvers to ensure consistency:

All should return the same thing (allowing for TTL differences).

Let's say you're operating a public website at the apex, want to delegate the web service cleanly, and still keep mail records at the same owner name. Here's what your zone could look like:

Your web origin can delegate HTTPS service metadata without sacrificing MX records. Supporting clients prefer the primary CDN metadata and can fall back to the secondary. Legacy clients still have ordinary A/AAAA fallback. The resolver-name SVCB records are separate: they help clients that already know resolver.company.example.com discover DoH and DoT.

This is simpler than trying to fake apex aliasing with CNAMEs, but it still needs realistic deployment hygiene: fallback A/AAAA for legacy clients, ordinary HTTPS redirects and HSTS for browsers that ignore HTTPS RRs, and a clear distinction between resolver-name discovery and _dns.resolver.arpa bootstrap DDR.

Monitor your HTTP/3 traffic ratio over time. Most analytics providers show this. When you publish HTTPS records with alpn="h3,h2", you may see HTTP/3 adoption climb noticeably on clients that honour the records.

From a service provider perspective, SVCB and HTTPS records can reduce recovery time during incidents. If your primary endpoint fails, participating clients already know about the secondary and can fall back without waiting for the next DNS publishing cycle. Your records define the preference order:

Most clients try priority 1 first and can fail over when that endpoint is unreachable. Some implementations may even probe more than one option in parallel, but you should treat that as an implementation detail rather than a universal guarantee.

ISPs and managed security providers can benefit from ipv4hint and ipv6hint parameters when the target name is separate from the owner name. These hints can reduce follow-up address lookups for clients that honor them:

With hints, supporting clients can often skip steps 2 and 3. The hints are advisory rather than mandatory, but they can still reduce resolver load and shave time off connection setup.

Organisations requiring encrypted DNS can use SVCB for resolver-name discovery when the resolver name is already known through DNR, manual configuration, or device management:

That is different from _dns.resolver.arpa, which is the bootstrap DDR query used when the client initially knows only a plaintext resolver IP. In both cases, supporting clients can discover encrypted transports without a hardcoded DoH URL, but automatic use still depends on client behavior and validation rules.

SVCB and HTTPS are standardized in RFC 9460. RFC 9461 defines the DNS-server mapping including dohpath, and RFC 9462 defines DDR. Adoption is strong among infrastructure providers, but client behavior still varies.

DNSSEC matters. Signing SVCB and HTTPS records helps protect clients from tampering and downgrade attacks. Check your records:

If RRSIG appears, signatures are published. If you query a validating resolver and see the ad flag, validation succeeded for that response.

Backward compatibility is built in. Old clients simply ignore these records and fall back to standard connections. No breaking changes. No legacy client pain.

Start simple, validate with real clients, and treat these records as an optimization layer rather than a magic replacement for every existing control.

For most organisations, SVCB and HTTPS records are unambiguously good. But there's a significant operational class where they present real problems: organisations trying to maintain control over encrypted DNS at their network perimeter.

Recall from the encrypted DNS post: supporting browsers and operating systems can query _dns.resolver.arpa to ask "where's your encrypted DNS endpoint?" SVCB records provide the answer. A client that gets a plaintext resolver from DHCP may then discover encrypted transports and, if its validation rules are satisfied, upgrade without an administrator explicitly entering a DoH URL.

When clients implement it, this can happen transparently. The user usually does not see it. The administrator may not see it either. Traffic analytics show HTTPS on port 443, which is so common it can disappear into the background. Your carefully planned encrypted DNS perimeter control can quietly stop working.

From a network security and compliance perspective, this is a problem. Your organisation decides all internal DNS should flow through your resolver with all the visibility and threat intelligence that entails. SVCB-based discovery can undermine that decision at the protocol level.

This behaviour is intentional. RFC 9461 and RFC 9462 explicitly define how DNS clients can learn encrypted resolver transports and parameters without manual endpoint configuration. The goal is to make encrypted DNS easier to discover and deploy, not something that only works after hand-entering a DoH URL.

This is a reasonable security goal, because encrypted DNS is more private than plaintext. But it conflicts directly with the security goal of network administrators who want to inspect DNS for threats.

The standard mitigation is what I mentioned in the encrypted DNS post: block SVCB and HTTPS record types at your internal resolver. Infoblox Advanced DNS Protection (ADP) does this by default with four blocking rules:

If clients never receive SVCB responses, they can't discover external DoH endpoints. They can't auto-upgrade. Your resolver remains the path of least resistance.

But this isn't a complete solution. It addresses auto-discovery but not clients with hardcoded DoH endpoints. A browser with https://1.1.1.1/dns-query baked in will use it regardless of SVCB records. Blocking SVCB is structural defence against auto-discovery, not perimeter defence.

SVCB records expose a deeper tension in network architecture: what layer owns DNS policy?

DNS layer perspective: SVCB records are just DNS records. They're published by domain owners. Blocking them feels like censoring published information.

Network perimeter perspective: SVCB records are a bypass mechanism. They're infrastructure that circumvents network policy. Blocking them feels like basic access control.

Both perspectives are technically correct. They're in direct conflict.

An organisation enforcing encrypted DNS at the perimeter, blocking port 853, blocking known DoH provider IPs, and filtering SNI on port 443, is implementing a deliberate security policy. SVCB records are a vector for that policy to be circumvented.

Conversely, a user who wants privacy is entitled to it. Blocking SVCB records to prevent privacy-seeking behaviour is ethically arguable.

Blocking SVCB records at the resolver helps. But complete control requires multiple layers:

No single layer is sufficient. SVCB records are just one part of a larger problem.

This depends on your security posture and threat model:

Both are defensible. The key is making the decision consciously, understanding the trade-offs, and implementing the mitigation layers that choice requires.

title: Wales win fourth Commonwealth Games swimming medal
description: Wales claim a fourth Commonwealth Games medal in the pool as the 4x200m freestyle relay team won another bronze.
fullText:
Wales claimed a fourth Commonwealth Games medal in the pool as the 4x200m freestyle relay team won another bronze.

Matt Richards and Dan Jones followed up the bronze they won in the 4x100m mixed freestyle relay, linking up with Kieran Bird and Tyler Melbourne-Smith to beat Scotland onto the podium.

Australia secured gold with a Commonwealth Games record time of seven minutes and 1.47 seconds, while England were second, a touch under five seconds quicker than Wales.

The two relay medals go alongside the silver and bronze won by Para-swimmers Ela Letton-Jones and Rhys Darbey respectively.

All four of Wales' medals have come in the pool, with Olympic gymnast Ruby Evans failing to finish on the podium in the women's all-round individual final on Sunday evening.

Wales are still waiting for that elusive gold medal after three days of competition in Glasgow.

"It's such a special group," said Richards.

"We've talked a lot about how tight-knit we are and a lot of us have come through the ranks since we were very young and grown as a team.

"To be able to do it together has been incredible.

"Seeing that Welsh flag go up when we're up on the podium is one of the highlights of my career so far.

"So hopefully we can do it a few more times."

Melbourne-Smith, who had been disqualified in the 4x100m relay on the opening day, brought Wales home on the final leg as he avoided being caught by Scotland home favourite Duncan Scott.

"My adrenaline was rushing but it was just about keeping it for the last 50 metres," said Melbourne-Smith.

"Holding my nerve, and that's what I did. These boys did all the hard work. For me, it was just about getting the job done.

"It's probably the best moment of my swimming career so far. It is unbelievable and I'm happy to do it with these boys."

Wales at the Commonwealth Games

Bird was on the podium after previously being part of the mixed freestyle relay quartet that swam in the heats.

Harry Milne, Jack Knight, Lewis Fraser and Bird had competed in the heats of the 4x200m freestyle relay on Sunday morning.

Fraser later finished seventh in his 100m butterfly final.

"When they asked me to step up for the team I didn't even hesitate," said Fraser.

"I know that's an individual event for me, but I always swim with the team on my back."

Theodora Taylor continued her impressive display in the pool by qualifying for the women's 100m freestyle final.

The 17-year-old, who won a relay bronze on Saturday, swam the fourth fastest time to make it through to Monday night's final.

Sophie Davies did not qualify despite a season's best, while Kyle Booth bowed out in the men's 50m breaststroke semi-final.

Meghan Willis finished sixth in the women's S9 100m backstroke final, won by England's Alice Tai.

title: McClements 'got everything perfect' on way to silver medal
description: Para-swimmer Barry McClements claims a Commonwealth Games silver medal in the men's S9 100m backstroke at Tollcross Swimming Centre.
fullText:
Para-swimmer Barry McClements claimed a Commonwealth Games silver medal in the men's S9 100m backstroke at Tollcross Swimming Centre.

It's Northern Ireland's second medal of the Games in Glasgow after Bethany Firth took bronze on Saturday in the women's S14 100m freestyle.

McClements, who won the bronze four years ago in the same event in Birmingham, pushed Australia's Timothy Hodge all the way to the touch, finishing in a time of 1:03.68, just 0.68 behind the Australian.

"This morning it was about just being comfortable, leaving a bit in the tank for this evening. I had a bit of a slip on the start this morning, so it didn't exactly go to plan so I knew there was a lot in the tank going into tonight, and I think, I got everything perfect," McClements told BBC Sport NI.

"It means a lot. We don't get to represent Northern Ireland unless we're at the Commonwealth Games.

"So just, again, to put our wee country on the map, it's the biggest privilege there is, I think, in swimming."

The two-time Paralympian was a step higher on the podium than he was four years ago and was proud of what he’s been able to achieve.

"My career has just been like stepping stones. Last year there was a bit of a step back, but sometimes you need to go backwards to go forwards.

"But again, I said it four years ago in Birmingham, I still just feel like a normal lad from Newtownards, and I'm just chasing my dream."

Daughter Charlotte inspires Firth to bronze medal

The Commonwealth Games allows for para-swimming events to be incorporated into the swimming programme and both McClements and Firth - a six-time Paralympic champion - have medalled at the last two Games, proving inspirational to many people who have a disability that they can achieve anything.

"That's the main aim," added McClements.

"No matter what obstacles you face, like, no matter where you grow up, disability or not, dream big and don't stop chasing your dreams."

McClements will now turn his attention to preparing for what’s ahead and will hopefully include the Paralympics in Los Angeles in two years time.

"Yeah, LA is the aim. Not sure what will happen after that, but, you know, just keep stepping up every year into LA and just see how fast I can go there."

McClements also believes the future for Northern Ireland is bright.

This is his third Commonwealth Games and he sees the level of performance just continues to rise.

"I was at the Gold Coast eight years ago and every Commonwealth Games, the team just keeps getting bigger and better.

"You know, the next Commonwealth Games could be a really, really, really good one for Northern Ireland. It's such a young team as well, and it's only up from here for Northern Ireland.

"For such a small country, to have this many good swimmers. It's pretty insane."

description: Adam Ramsay-Peaty qualifies for the 50m breaststroke final with the third fastest time at the Commonwealth Games.
fullText:
England's Adam Ramsay-Peaty will have the chance to defend his men's 50m breaststroke title at the Commonwealth Games after qualifying third fastest for the final.

The 31-year-old, who broke down in tears after taking bronze in the 100m on Saturday night, finished second in his semi-final with a time of 26.82 seconds.

World record holder Ramsay-Peaty will have to close the gap to South Africa's Michael Houlie - who set the pace with 26.61 - when he races in the final on Monday at 20:07 BST.

Australia's 100m breaststroke gold medallist Sam Williamson and Jersey's silver medallist Filip Nowacki will also line up in the final.

"I think I've still got a little bit more to grow. I think there was a massive lesson in yesterday," three-time Olympic gold medallist Ramsay-Peaty told BBC Sport.

"I can't change anything obviously, so we have to get over it. I also know the trajectory I have to be on now and it's a little bit different to what I thought it was.

"I've also got to remind myself that I haven't swam a championships in two years. I put a lot of expectation on myself coming into this games.

"But as you know, the best athletes in the world, you don't do it in training, you have to actually compete well and that is a skill on its own and we have to get used to that.

"I'm enjoying it and we'll have to see what that result is tomorrow."

Ramsay-Peaty's team-mate Max Morgan finished sixth in the same semi-final race and was eliminated.

fullText:

Australia's Lucas Herbert swept to victory on the final day of the LIV UK event in Staffordshire.

The 30-year-old led throughout at the JCB Golf and Country Club in Rocester and carried a three-shot advantage over Bryson DeChambeau into the final round.

And the world number 69 rammed home his dominance on Sunday by firing the round of the day - a 10-under 62 - to finish on 30-under overall.

Herbert won by six strokes from England's Tyrrell Hatton, who shot a 63, while American DeChambeau finished three shots further back in third.

It was Herbert's second LIV victory of the year and his 30-under finish was the lowest in the tour's five-year history.

Last week the Australian finished in a tie for sixth in the Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, four shots behind winner Ryan Fox.

"I just wanted to carry that into this week the best I could," said Herbert.

"It was good to play like that today when I was being pushed by two of the best players in the world."

Hatton, who won the previous LIV event in Andalucia, added: "I wanted to get off to a fast start, which is what I did, but unfortunately Lucas did as well.

"It would have been amazing to win in front of home fans, but I tried my best. Lucas was incredible this week."

title: Lifting the 'Mayo curse' - what it meant to end 75 years of All-Ireland hurt
description: After Mayo ended their 75-year wait to win the All-Ireland, what does it mean to finally end the 'Mayo curse'?.
fullText:
When the full-time hooter sounded at Croke Park on Sunday, there was a noise to rival any in the historic past of the iconic Dublin stadium.

It was the sound of the end of 75 years of hurt and heartbreak, of near-misses and misplaced hope.

After all that time, Mayo had finally won the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship - a fourth in their history, but one three-quarters of a century in the making.

The players sunk to their knees on the hallowed turf, fully aware of what they had just accomplished.

Not only had they dethroned Kerry, the favourites to win consecutive All-Ireland titles and the sport's most decorated team, but they had ended the so-called 'Mayo Curse', which had lingered over the county since 1951.

It was a day of history, a day of ecstasy and, to some degree, a day of relief.

With tears in his eyes, former Mayo defender Padraig O'Hora - working as a pundit for the BBC - said he "can't put it into words".

"Thousands upon thousands of people have dreamed of this day, I can't believe it's here," he said.

"There are people who have waited their whole lives for this.

"Hats off to the lads on the field, it is their day, but if you have green and red blood it belongs to you, young and old.

"What a moment for Gaelic football, what a moment for sport. It's just something else."

Pride and emotion as Mayo end 75-year wait for glory

Mayo beat Kerry in thriller to end 75-year All-Ireland wait

Cursed? The story of the 72-year-old hex that haunts Mayo

To understand the significance of Mayo's victory on Sunday, you have to go back to 1951.

In a world still reeling from the effects of the Second World War, Harry S Truman was US president as Cold War tensions started to rise, while Winston Churchill was Prime Minister.

Culturally, Nat King Cole and BB King were some of the biggest music artists, while Alice in Wonderland and A Streetcar Named Desire were on the big screen.

That year, Mayo lifted the Sam Maguire Cup - the iconic trophy presented to the team that wins the All-Ireland SFC - for the third time, but it was the celebrations after that caused a stir.

As is so often the case, the players enjoyed themselves. But on their way home they passed a funeral in the village of Foxford, where a local priest reportedly accused the Mayo team of not showing respect.

Instead of stopping and switching off their engine, as would have been the custom in rural Ireland at the time, the Mayo party continued.

In return - legend has it - the priest placed a curse on Mayo, saying they would never win another All-Ireland while any of the players on the panel were still alive.

It has never been established if the event actually occurred, but after 11 All-Ireland finals came, went and ended in defeat, the myth of the curse grew.

Just two weeks after their previous final defeat by Tyrone in 2021, Paddy Prendergast, the last player to feature in the 1951 final, passed away aged 95.

Two years later, Dr Mick Loftus - the last surviving squad member - died aged 93, but it would not be until this year that Mayo returned to the biggest stage in Irish sport.

It looked like Mayo would be on the end of another defeat when David Clifford - widely considered one of the greatest players of his generation, perhaps even of all time - netted to put Kerry in control in the early stages.

But Mayo dug deep and fought back, and trailed by a single point at half-time.

Things changed four minutes after the restart when Darragh Beirne finished off a flowing move to put Mayo into a lead they would not relinquish.

Kerry, as great champions do, never folded and there was a late scare as the pressure grew, but Mayo were not to be denied in a three-point victory.

The tears and emotion at the final whistle meant everything.

Manager Andy Moran, a former Mayo player and in his first year in charge, went to his wife and family in the stands.

The new generation, such as Beirne and the superb Aussie Rules-bound Kobe McDonald, soaked in every moment on the Croke Park pitch.

There was over 80,000 people in attendance, and for those in green and red, plus the many neutrals in attendance, there was barely a dry eye in the house.

While the so-called 'curse' is one thing, Mayo also wore a special white jersey in a final for the first time since 1951 due to a clash between the green home kit of Kerry. Perhaps it was fate.

"To every man, women, boy and girl in Mayo, wherever you are, dream big things," said captain Jack Coyne, who delivered one of the all-time great speeches before lifting the Sam Maguire.

"Anything is possible and we've shown it today. I'm over the moon."

For McDonald, only 18 and whose father Ciaran featured in All-Ireland final heartbreaks, was able to sum up what it means to win the All-Ireland.

Just finished his end-of-school leaving cert exams, he will move to Australia to join St Kilda in the lucrative Australian Football League.

Given Gaelic football is an amateur sport, it is something he cannot be offered at home but he was determined to make history with 'one chance' written on his wrist before his Australian adventure.

In the All-Ireland, players play for the counties they are born in. That's why it means more.

"It's surreal, we don't know how to feel," McDonald said on the GAA Social.

"To look around and see the people, they have given us so much over the years and to give them something proper to shout about is special."

When asked if he knew what lay ahead in the celebrations, he added: "I don't, but I can't wait to find out.

"We'll soak it in and enjoy it."

Mayo will now head back to Castlebar in their home county to celebrate their historic success with their people.

Given it took 75 years, there is set to be another sea of celebration when they arrive on Ireland's west coast.

Let's just hope they avoid any funerals on the journey home.

title: AI Can Ride My Bike with No Handlebars
description: A 2008 alt-hip-hop hit holds the perfect warning for the artificial intelligence arms race and how big tech is weaponizing sci-fi hypotheticals to distract us from their own unchecked corporate power.
fullText:
I don’t remember the first time I heard Flobot’s Handlebars, but I have been hearing it a lot again recently in an attempt to connect with my past.

The song’s lyrics start with someone expressing happiness at the fact that they can ride a bicycle with no handlebars, and by the end, they threaten to end the world in a holocaust. There can be several interpretations of what any lyrics mean, but in this case, we can find a quote from the artist that clarifies the intended meaning:

The song is about the idea that we have so much incredible potential as human beings to be destructive or to be creative. And it’s tragic to me that the appetite for military innovation is endless, but when it comes to taking on a project like ending world hunger, it’s seen as outlandish. It’s not treated with the same seriousness… We have these little moments of creativity, these bursts of innovation, and every time that happens, that innovation is used to oppress and destroy people.

The song speaks about how scale almost always corrupts human innovation; that the same core innovation spirit in us that lets us find meaning and joy in simple acts like riding a bicycle with no handlebars can bring us meaning (and in some cases, joy) of guiding a missile with no satellite; that the human ego at scale is a dangerous thing.

Which brings us to the world of AI. Scale is everything in the world of artificial intelligence today, and it has been a big data center contest lately. The companies behind the frontier models have also scaled to extreme massive levels, with valuations hovering around hundreds of billions of dollars.

Perhaps the song is quite fitting for this narrative as well.

AI CEOs love talking about the end of the world for some reason. Another unqualified thing they often talk about is consciousness, with many frontier labs hinting that consciousness is just another milestone on the AI development roadmap, i.e., not only could their models represent and mimic people but actually be people. Almost all of them do not ponder much the ethical and moral implications of a truly conscious being in this context.

I think AI will probably, like, most likely sort of lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there will be great companies created with serious machine learning.

The idea that intelligent machines will destroy the world is not new. Many sci-fi works explore the situation; most involve a hyper-intelligent system that is either fully conscious as a being or can act as if it is. Most of them will not explain how it works, in the sense of how these computers or software turned into this thing.

The thing just shows up buck naked in a bar with a German accent and demands your clothes. It doesn’t tell you, “Oh yes, I understand what you’re saying and why you shall be curious. Yes, please sit down while I give you a presentation going through everything, all the scientific progress we made, how the machines actually work, what is consciousness and how we manipulate it, and et cetera.” That would make for a very boring movie.

Once we build a generally intelligent system, that basically we will ask it to figure out a way to make an investment return for you.

Consciousness is a subject that always seems to be at the center of the AI discussion but is never discussed seriously. For example, a tech CEO might boldly proclaim that their company will reach AGI (in fact, a specific form of conscious AGI) in the next three years. However, instead of following through on the legal, ethical, and philosophical framework of the company owning conscious beings, they would move on to how their ad business did 5% more year-over-year.

But is consciousness required or a part of the definition of AGI? The consensus seems to say no.

In recent times, we’ve also seen some pullback in the rhetoric, with leaders trying to define AGI as a capacity threshold rather than a claim of consciousness. For example, last year Sam Altman said: “I think it’s not a super useful term” when talking about AGI. It would be fair to assume that, instead of creating a living, breathing digital dog (which presumably is not just a matter of compute), the focus is now on creating a system that can replace human labor effectively, at least.

While a non-conscious AI system that can perform human tasks at a superlative capacity will mean you don’t need to worry about ethical and moral issues of deploying the said AI, it would still be a dangerous thing for society at large, just not in a Skynet type of way.

In his essay “The Adolescence of Technology”, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proclaims seriously, “humanity is about to be handed almost unimaginable power, and it is deeply unclear whether we possess the maturity to wield it.” Most of the essay seems to be an argument for more regulations on AI; you can read it at your own risk and make up your mind on it.

Either way, skynet or no skynet, we can assume that if the AI arms race goes well, then in the worst case (from the point of view of AI companies) is that LLMs do not gain consciousness with more compute, but with better harnesses and integration, AI can become genuinely useful in every field to the point where the “controllers” of AI, i.e. the companies that control them, will be given an almost unimaginable power and it is deeply unclear if they have the maturity to wield it.

At that point, the worries expressed by Mr. Amodei in his essay become realistic concerns for everyone. However, if his answer can be found in the blog post that starts with “There is a scene in the movie version of Carl Sagan’s book Contact where the main character, an astronomer…”, I deem it not serious enough. By framing his essay with a romanticized sci-fi reference to the movie Contact, Amodei treats an immediate geopolitical and economic crisis as a philosophical thought experiment, skipping over the difficult questions of accountability. (I know that sounds rich coming from the person whose entire hook of the article is an late 2000s rap song, but still.)

Even on a rudimentary reading, he skips most of the difficult questions and focuses on things like billionaire philanthropy and preventing hardware access to oh-so-evil China. It is a great answer if you’re a billionaire and control the said AI, but it would be possible to argue that it is not the best answer, or the most ethical answer, or the fairest answer for all.

This brings me back to the song, and these particular lines:

I can hand out a million vaccinations / Or let ‘em all die in exasperation / Have ‘em all healed from their lacerations / Or have ‘em all killed by assassination / I can make anybody go to prison / Just because I don’t like ‘em / And I can do anything with no permission

A world where that stands true for private US companies like Google, OpenAI, Amazon, Anthropic, or any private company does not sound like a good world. And it might be the world we are heading towards, AGI or no AGI.

It is a bit funny how tech CEOs will often claim that artificial intelligence, “the AI”, will take away x percent of jobs in y years. But they never say that their company will do it; they never say they’re investing billions hoping this happens, but rather “the AI” will take away the jobs and replace human beings, and we must be forewarned about such an evil winter that is to fall upon us.

Yet, from what we can see, there is no difference between OpenAI and the models it runs behind its closed doors, and the same for every private frontier AI lab. Yet there seems to be a sense that it’s acceptable to attribute full agency to the AI when it’s convenient while you own the shares and all financial gains.

You blame the same demon you command and profit from.

The moral problem in AI in this case isn’t really whether AI can be conscious or how to live in a world where that is true. But rather, should we trust in AI labs to be worthy of wielding such power? History tells us that no private entity is worthy of that power.

title: After chaotic return, where does Joshua win leave Fury fight?
description: Where does Anthony Joshua's chaotic comeback win over Kristian Prenga leave the super-fight with Tyson Fury?
fullText:
After just 20 seconds, the biggest fight in British boxing had seemingly gone up in smoke in Jeddah's desert air.

Anthony Joshua was flat on his back and a long-awaited showdown with Tyson Fury was hanging in the balance.

One more knockdown, one astonishing comeback and a second-round knockout later, the blockbuster bout was revived.

But after one of the wildest nights of Joshua's career against Kristian Prenga, the Fury fight suddenly feels like a very different contest.

"That was chaos. Absolute chaos. Just madness," former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew said on DAZN.

Joshua's emotional win over Prenga in pictures

Relive Joshua's dramatic comeback knockout win

Bloodied Kelly battles past Agyarko to retain title

The emotion of Joshua's comeback victory cannot be overstated. Given everything he has endured since the tragic car crash in Nigeria that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele, simply stepping back into the ring was an achievement.

Sentiment aside, though, had Albanian Prenga pressed home his advantage after dropping Joshua twice in the opening round, the story could have been very different.

Prenga arrived with an impressive record - 20 knockouts from 20 victories and one defeat - but had never operated anywhere near this level or under this kind of spotlight.

"I think we need to look at that first round and look at how easily AJ was hurt. We can't just skip past that," 5 Live boxing pundit Steve Bunce said.

"We saw a man in a very bad place come through an even worse situation and emerge victorious at the end. That will be the story.

"However, once we step back, we need to keep looking at that first round and start asking: how much further do we want to push him?"

This was supposed to be Joshua's comeback week. Instead, Fury reminded everyone that he remains the master of stealing a headline.

Fury was originally expected to fight on 1 August in Dublin, but moved quickly to schedule his own bout against a 46-year-old Mariusz Wach for the evening before Joshua's fight night.

Then in fight week came the usual Fury theatre. He insisted he would not be in Jeddah, before hinting the opposite. An Instagram post tagged with the location "Who Knows" only added fuel to the speculation.

In the end, Fury stayed away and perhaps that was a blessing for Joshua. Had Fury been sitting ringside watching his rival get dropped twice in the opening round, would Joshua have found the same reserves of determination to turn the fight around? Would the pressure of knowing Fury was watching have changed the moment?

We will never know. But what we do know is that while the two men made it through their respective warm-ups, questions remain after both performances.

Fury's seventh-round victory over Wach was heavily criticised by some but it was effectively a public sparring session designed to keep Fury active and keep his name in the conversation.

There was little jeopardy involved and Fury appeared to be enjoying himself, even sharing a playful moment by kissing his opponent on the head.

Perhaps we should read more into his performance against Arslanbek Makhmudov in April where Fury - while still showing signs of decline - looked comfortable and controlled.

Fury's greatest weapon has always been his ability to expose hesitation, vulnerability and mistakes - and Joshua showed all three against Prenga.

In the aftermath of such a chaotic night, it is easy to focus only on the flaws and forget the bigger picture. Joshua was returning from one of the darkest periods of his life and carrying an immense emotional burden into the ring.

After his hand was raised, he struggled to get through his interview. His voice cracked as he spoke about his two friends and the impact their loss has had on him.

"Boxing once saved him and he needed boxing to get through this. That camp allowed him to focus his mind while he was in so much grief and pain," promoter Eddie Hearn said.

"You don't know what he was going through in that camp because he doesn't talk about it."

Whatever happens next, his place in British boxing history is already secure. He is an Olympic gold medallist, a two-time heavyweight champion and one of the biggest sporting stars this country has produced.

He has taken boxing to places few British fighters ever have. He has filled stadiums, headlined global events and become a household name far beyond the sport.

But in the build-up to his comeback, Joshua and his stablemate Oleksandr Usyk spoke about the ambition of becoming undisputed heavyweight champion.

After Saturday night in Saudi, the reality is that even reclaiming a world title would be a tough ask.

Joshua has always spoken about legacy, and there would be something fitting about walking away after overcoming one of the toughest periods of his life and producing a dramatic comeback victory.

The danger with ageing fighters is chasing one more night. Boxing history is filled with champions who stayed that one fight too long.

But then again Fury-Joshua is not one more fight. It is the fight. The one that has loomed over their careers for the best part of a decade.

title: McInnes teases Rangers signing within 48 hours
description: Rangers hope to announce another signing within 48 hours, with manager Derek McInnes teasing a second by the time his side open their season away to Dundee United on Friday.
fullText:
Rangers hope to announce another signing within 48 hours, with manager Derek McInnes teasing a second by the time his side open their season away to Dundee United on Friday.

But Nicolas Raskin will not be involved as the Belgium midfielder is only expected back from his break after the World Cup this week and with Rangers anticipating transfer interest in the 25-year-old.

Rangers have already brought in seven new players this summer, but a defender and winger appear to be McInnes' priorities.

"We are quite hopeful we've got one done at the minute and hopefully we'll have some news on that in the next 48 hours and we're also trying to maybe bring one

"I would really like that to be the case because I do think it one or two areas of the pitch we're still a bit short.

"One will be permanent, one might be a loan, but we would like two permanent."

McInnes lamented the lack of chances created in Sunday's final pre-season friendly - a goalless draw at home to West Ham United.

"It is just those difference makers," he said. "I think a club like ours needs to have those guys who can isolate and go one v one and can play off both sides.

"So we are looking for a bit more creativity that can serve the strikers.

"I think we've got strikers in Nadiri, Chermiti, Shankland and Miovski who can all finish off chances.

"Maybe only Chermiti is capable of creating an opportunity for himself. But Ryan, Lawrence and Bojan are very much dependent on service."

Meanwhile, McInnes feels "a bit short in terms of numbers defensively" with four games in 12 days.

"I think we had five senior defenders available there and Ross McCrorie's just opened up his knee a bit and we didn't take any risk with him today," he said.

Rangers have signed three defensive midfielders this summer in anticipation of selling Raskin.

Asked if the Belgian would be involved at Tannadice, McInnes said: "Not for the opening part of the season he won't, but going forward, Nico might be subject to some interest, we are well aware of that.

"We always thought he could be a flight risk this summer on the back of the World Cup, so we've reinforced the midfield area.

"But obviously if nothing comes in for Nico then it's another good player to add to it."

Asked if there were any imminent outgoings, McInnes added: "There's been a wee bit of interest in one or two without naming names."

American rookie Jackson Koivun held his nerve to beat Scottie Scheffler by three strokes and claim his first PGA Tour win at the 3M Open on Sunday.

Playing in just his third tournament since turning professional, Koivun surged into a three-shot lead on Saturday during a round of 10-under 61.

The 21-year-old then stretched his lead to five in the final round at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, before world number one Scheffler applied pressure.

The four-time major winner began the back nine with three straight birdies, then claimed two 

Former world amateur number one Koivun could have wobbled at that point, with holes left to play, but instead he made his fifth birdie of the day at 16 before wrapping up a five-under 66 to finish on 25 under par overall.

"I had some nerves coming down 18," said Koivun. "All throughout the crowd I kept hearing 'Scottie's coming, Scottie's coming'.

"I just tried to tune that out and keep playing the golf I knew I could and was able to find some good putts coming down the stretch."

American trio Denny McCarthy, Brian Harman and Chandler Phillips finished five strokes behind Koivun, in a tie for third with Japan's Hideki Matsuyama.

Michael Kim fired a 12-under 59 on Friday, but the American finished in a tie for 10th after closing with rounds of 70 and 69.
